# The problem {#sec-lf-problem}

This document describes the manufactured problems with which cardiacFoam
verifies the lead-field ECG: the ECG domain `leadFieldECG`, whose channels
are built from the lead fields of the utility `buildLeadFields`. In the
method of manufactured solutions [@roache2002code] an exact field is chosen
first and the data that make it satisfy the equations are derived from it.
The document gives, for each problem, the geometry and its regions, the
conductivities, the exact heart transmembrane potential and torso potential,
the electrodes, the reference point that fixes the constant of the
potential, the meshes, and the quantities the verifier compares. It states
the problems only; it contains no solver output. Every displayed field,
conductivity, source and constant of the exact solutions is printed by the
sympy generator of its problem, `slab_leadfield_mms.py` or `shell_mms.py`. A
reader with this document, the generator folder and the tutorial cases can
rebuild each problem in another code.

## Domain and governing equations

The conductor is the heart $\Omega_H$ (the cellZone `myocardium`) and the
torso $\Omega_T$ (the bath cellZones of the ECG domain), with the interface
$\Gamma=\partial\Omega_H\cap\partial\Omega_T$. For a given transmembrane
potential $V_m$ in the heart, the passive potential $\phi$ solves

$$
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
\nabla\cdot\big((\mathbf G_i+\mathbf G_e)\nabla\phi\big)
&=-\nabla\cdot(\mathbf G_i\nabla V_m)+S_H
&&\text{in }\Omega_H,\\
\nabla\cdot(\sigma\nabla\phi)&=S_T&&\text{in }\Omega_T,\\
\phi\ \text{continuous},\quad
\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf G_w\nabla\phi
&=\mathbf n\cdot\sigma\nabla\phi&&\text{on }\Gamma,\\
\mathbf n\cdot\sigma\nabla\phi&=g_{\mathrm{out}}&&\text{on }\partial\Omega_T\setminus\Gamma,
\end{aligned}
\right.
$$

where $S_H$, $S_T$ and $g_{\mathrm{out}}$ are manufactured data (zero in
ordinary runs).
The heart source is assembled with no wall flux of $\mathbf G_i\nabla V_m$.
The heart-side wall conductivity $\mathbf G_w$ is the conductor's choice: with
a monodomain myocardium, whose $V_m$ is sealed
($\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf G_i\nabla V_m=0$), the wall carries the total
conductivity, $\mathbf G_w=\mathbf G_i+\mathbf G_e$; with a bidomain
myocardium the intracellular potential is sealed,
$\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf G_i\nabla(\phi+V_m)=0$, and
$\mathbf G_w=\mathbf G_e$. The problem is of pure Neumann
type; the constant of $\phi$ is fixed by a reference point
$\mathbf r_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in the torso (`phiERefPoint` of the torso
dictionary), whose cell is pinned to the reference value
$\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}=0$.

The ECG of electrode $e$ at $\mathbf r_e$ is the value of $\phi$ in the cell
$c(e)$ that contains $\mathbf r_e$. The lead-field ECG computes it from the
lead field of the electrode, the solution of the adjoint discrete problem,
without solving for $\phi$ at each sample [@geselowitz1967bioelectric];
@sec-identity states the identity and what is compared. Electrodes lie in the
torso: `buildLeadFields` and `leadFieldECG` stop with a fatal error when an
electrode cell is a heart cell. Each case has two kinds of electrode, recorded
in the same way. The eight body-surface electrodes `surface1` to `surface8`
lie just inside the outer boundary of the conductor, in cells with a face on
it; they are the ECG. The interior probes lie inside the torso, in the bath
ball or next to the heart, and test the same channel where the potential and
its error differ from those at the surface.

The equations use SI units with lengths and times normalised by
$1\,\mathrm m$ and $1\,\mathrm s$, so the arguments of the trigonometric,
exponential and square-root functions are dimensionless.

## Reading and regenerating {#sec-lf-regenerate}

The generators live in `tutorials/manufacturedSolutions/generators/` of the
cardiacFoam repository. The slab and layered potentials (@sec-slab) are
closed forms in one variable, built by `slab_leadfield_mms.py`, which writes
`reference/slab_leadfield.py` and `latex/leadfield_*.tex`. The
curved-conductor potential (@sec-shell) is the transmission solution of
`shell_mms.py`, which writes `latex/shell_transmission_*.tex` and the C++
header `manufacturedShellTransmissionBathBidomainReference.H` of
`src/verificationModels/bathBidomainVerification/`.

Set up the environment once and run a generator from that folder:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python slab_leadfield_mms.py --emit
.venv/bin/python slab_leadfield_mms.py --self-check
```

`--emit` runs the self-checks first and writes nothing if one fails;
`--self-check` runs them alone. `shell_mms.py` also takes `--check PATH` and
`--write PATH`, which compare or rewrite its C++ header and are needed only by
cardiacFoam developers. `docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py` holds what
depends on the tutorial cases and on finished runs:

```bash
python docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py --self-check
python docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py --check-run RUN
```

`--self-check` asserts that the electrodes and reference points of the cases
lie where @sec-slab and @sec-shell place them. `--check-run RUN` reads a
finished run of a lead-field tutorial (its `log.cardiacFoam`,
`postProcessing/manufacturedLeadFieldECG_ECG.dat` and `constant/polyMesh`)
and compares the exact columns written by the verifier with the exact
potentials (@sec-slab-checks, @sec-shell-checks). The document is built with

```bash
quarto render docs/leadField/leadField_mms.qmd --to pdf
```

and its figures with `python docs/leadField/figures.py`, which takes
`--draft`, `--outdir DIR` and `--mesh-case NAME=PATH` (names `slab_hex`,
`slab_tet`, `layered_hex`, `layered_tet`, `shell_hex`, `shell_tet`) as the
monodomain figure script does.

# Insulated slab and layered torso {#sec-slab}

## Description and limitations

A heart slab between two torso slabs, with a one-dimensional exact solution
along $x$. The tutorial is `manufacturedSolutions/leadFieldECG`, with two
exact solutions selected by `-problem`:

- `slab`: every outer face is insulated. The torso potential is constant in
  each torso slab, so the ECG between the slabs is known exactly and does not
  depend on the torso conductivity. These are the fields of the FDA bath slab
  of the bath-bidomain tutorial with the bath current set to zero.
- `layered`: each torso slab is split into two layers of different
  conductivity, and a uniform current density crosses the whole box along
  $x$. The potential is then piecewise linear in the torso, with a change of
  slope at each layer interface and at each heart wall.

The heart runs the one-dimensional FDA monodomain or bidomain manufactured
field [@pathmanathan2013verification] on the three-dimensional heart mesh
(`dimension "1D"`), so the computed $V_m$ approximates the exact $V_m$
below and the lead-field and direct channels can be compared on it.

The problems exercise the heart source $-\nabla\cdot(\mathbf G_i\nabla V_m)$,
the heart and torso operators, two plane heart--torso interfaces and, in the
layered problem, two plane torso--torso interfaces with a conductivity ratio
of 5 and a current through all of them. They do not exercise a curved
interface, a varying torso conductivity, an off-diagonal conductivity or
an electrode where the exact potential varies across the slab's $y$ and $z$.
In the slab problem the exact torso potential is constant, so the point and
the centroid values of an electrode are equal and the torso conductivity does
not enter. The layered problem with a current needs the monodomain
myocardium: at the walls the exact heart slope $\alpha/(\mathbf G_i+\mathbf G_e)_{xx}$
carries the intracellular flux $\alpha G_{i,xx}/(G_{i,xx}+G_{e,xx})$, which the
sealed intracellular potential of the bidomain conductor does not admit.

## Problem instance

Box $[-1,2]\times[0,1]^2$: torso $-1\le x\le0$, heart $0\le x\le1$, torso
$1\le x\le2$ (@fig-slab-geometry). The heart conductivities are uniform and
diagonal (S m$^{-1}$):

| myocardium | conductivity | ECG domain $\mathbf G_i$ | ECG domain $\mathbf G_e$ |
|:------|:--------------------------|:--------|:--------|
| `monodomain` | $\mathbf G_m=\mathrm{diag}(0.111453302,\,0.121585420,\,0.030396355)$ | $(2+\sqrt2)\,\mathbf G_m$ | $\sqrt2\,\mathbf G_m$ |
| `bidomain` | $\mathbf G_i=\mathrm{diag}(0.111453302,\,0.121585420,\,0.030396355)$, $\mathbf G_e=\mathrm{diag}(0.046165469,\,0.050362330,\,0.012590582)$ | the solver's | the solver's |

In both rows $k=G_{i,xx}/(G_{i,xx}+G_{e,xx})=1/\sqrt2$. The exact solution
depends on the $xx$ entries only, so it is the same for the options
`-conductivity anisotropic`, `isotropic` and `unequal` of the tutorial; the
three differ in what the static error measures (tutorial README).

- `slab`: torso conductivity $\sigma$ in the cellZone `bath`; every outer
  face insulated ($g_{\mathrm{out}}=0$); $S_H=S_T=0$.
- `layered`: the torso slabs split at $x_L=-0.5$ and $x_R=1.5$ into the
  cellZones `torsoInner` ($x_L<x<0$ and $1<x<x_R$, $\sigma_1=0.1$) and
  `torsoOuter` ($x<x_L$ and $x>x_R$, $\sigma_2=0.02$); surface currents
  $\mathbf n\cdot\sigma\nabla\phi=-\alpha$ on the face `xMin` ($x=-1$) and
  $+\alpha$ on `xMax` ($x=2$), $\alpha=0.01$ (`-alpha`); the faces `sides`
  insulated. The current density $-\sigma\nabla\phi=-\alpha\,\mathbf e_x$ is
  the same in every layer.
- Reference point $\mathbf r_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in the left torso (the outer
  layer in `layered`), with the value $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The
  bidomain myocardium also pins its own heart potential at
  $(0.1137,\,0.0437,\,0.0437)$; that pin belongs to the heart solve and not
  to the conductor of the ECG domain.
- The constants:

{{< include ../../latex/leadfield_layered_params.tex >}}

## Construction

*Slab.* With $S=\sqrt{1+t}$, the heart field is the FDA field of $d=1$,
$V_m=S\cos(\pi x)$. Its derivative vanishes at $x=0$ and $x=1$, so no
current leaves the heart through $\Gamma$ whichever wall conductivity the
conductor uses. In the heart, $\phi=-kV_m+C$ solves
$\nabla\cdot((\mathbf G_i+\mathbf G_e)\nabla\phi)=-\nabla\cdot(\mathbf G_i\nabla V_m)$
because $\phi$ and $V_m$ depend on $x$ only and
$(G_{i,xx}+G_{e,xx})\,k=G_{i,xx}$. Its slope vanishes at both walls, so the
torso potential is constant on each side and continuity fixes it to the wall
value: $-kS+C$ on the left and $kS+C$ on the right. The torso conductivity
does not enter.

*Layered.* A uniform current density $-\alpha\,\mathbf e_x$ through layers
of conductivity $\sigma(x)$ ($\sigma_2$, $\sigma_1$,
$(G_i+G_e)_{xx}$, $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$ from left to right) has the
potential $\alpha R(x)$ with $R'=1/\sigma$. $R$ is continuous and
$\sigma R'=1$ in every layer, so the potential and the normal current are
continuous at $x=x_L,0,1,x_R$; on `xMin` the outward normal is
$-\mathbf e_x$ and $\mathbf n\cdot\sigma\nabla(\alpha R)=-\alpha$, on `xMax`
it is $+\alpha$. Adding $\alpha R$ to the slab potential leaves the heart
equation unchanged, because $R$ is linear in the heart, and $V_m$ is the
slab's. The sides stay insulated because the potential depends on $x$ only
and no tensor has $xy$ or $xz$ entries.

*Gauge.* The verifier evaluates the exact potential at a point
$\mathbf x$ as

$$
\phi(\mathbf x,t)=\phi^{\ast}(\mathbf x,t)-\phi^{\ast}(\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}},t)+\phi_{\mathrm{ref}},
$$

with $\phi^\ast$ the formula below and $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the
centroid of the cell that contains $\mathbf r_{\mathrm{ref}}$, the cell the
conductor pins. The constant $C$ of the formulas therefore cancels.

The verifier takes $\alpha$ from the surface currents and the four layer
conductivities from the torso cells, and stops with a fatal error when a torso
cell crosses a layer interface, when a layer has more than one or an
anisotropic conductivity, when the surface currents are not along $x$ or carry
a net current, or when a current is combined with the bidomain conductor.
With $\alpha=0$ the layered potential equals the slab's for any $\sigma_1$,
$\sigma_2$.

The full expressions are `fields()` of `slab_leadfield_mms.py` and `Vm`,
`phi_slab`, `resistance` and `phi_layered` of `reference/slab_leadfield.py`,
whose layer arguments carry each side separately (`sigmaOuterLeft`,
`sigmaInnerLeft`, `sigmaHeart`, `sigmaInnerRight`, `sigmaOuterRight`) as the
C++ structure does; `PARAMS` holds the values of the tutorial. In code, the
functions of `manufacturedLeadFieldECGReference.H`:

- `manufacturedLeadFieldSlabVm`;
- `manufacturedLeadFieldSlabPhi`, which calls `manufacturedFDABathPhiEAt`
  with the bath current 0 and $\sigma_e=1$;
- `manufacturedLeadFieldLayeredResistance`;
- `manufacturedLeadFieldLayeredPhi`;

and their transcription `slab_vm`, `slab_phi_raw`, `layered_resistance`,
`layered_phi_raw` and `gauged` of `docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py`,
which follows the header branch by branch.

## Self-checks {#sec-slab-checks}

`slab_leadfield_mms.py --self-check` asserts, symbolically:

- in the heart $(G_i+G_e)_{xx}\,\phi''=-G_{i,xx}V_m''$ with
  $k(G_i+G_e)_{xx}=G_{i,xx}$, and $V_m'$ vanishes at $x=0$ and $x=1$;
- $\phi^\ast_{\mathrm{slab}}$ is continuous at $x=0$ and $x=1$ and linear in
  each torso slab, and, gauged in the left torso, $0$ on the left and $2kS$
  on the right;
- $R$ is continuous at $x_L$, $0$, $1$, $x_R$, $R(0)=0$, and $\sigma R'=1$ in
  every layer, so the normal current is continuous;
- the surface currents are $-\alpha$ on $x=-1$ and $+\alpha$ on $x=2$;
- with $\alpha=0$ the layered potential equals the slab's;
- $k=1/\sqrt2$ to $10^{-8}$ for both conductivity pairs of the tutorial;
- the printed constants round-trip.

`test_slab_leadfield_mms.py` compares `reference/slab_leadfield.py` with
`leadfield_reference.py`, the transcription of the C++ header, to
$10^{-15}$ on $-1\le x\le2$ at three times, and the constants with the
dictionaries of the tutorial. `leadfield_reference.py --self-check` asserts
that $k=1/\sqrt2$ to $10^{-11}$; that $\phi^\ast_{\mathrm{slab}}$ is $0$ on
the left, $2kS$ on the right and continuous at $x=0$ and $x=1$; that $R$ is
continuous with $\sigma R'=1$ (central differences, $10^{-8}$) on both sides of
each of $x_L$, $0$, $1$, $x_R$; and that the electrodes of the case are
`surface1` to `surface8`, $0.003$ from the outer boundary, and probes
farther inside, all in the torso and none on a hexahedral face at
$N=10,20,40,80$.

`--check-run RUN` reads the verifier line of `log.cardiacFoam` (reference,
$k$, $\alpha$ and the layer conductivities, which must equal the values of
@sec-slab to the printed precision) and, at every sample, asserts to
$10^{-12}$ that:

- $\phi^\ast(\mathbf r_e,t)-\phi_{\mathrm{exactPoint},e}$ is one constant over
  the electrodes, the gauge;
- the gauge equals $\phi^\ast(\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}},t)$, with
  $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the centroid of the cell that contains
  $\mathbf r_{\mathrm{ref}}$;
- $\phi^\ast(\mathbf x_{c(e)},t)$ minus the gauge equals the column
  `exactCentroid` of each electrode.

The centroids are computed from the cell vertices in double precision; this
is exact for the axis-aligned hexahedra and for tetrahedra. On the meshes of
the figures below the largest differences are $3\times10^{-15}$ (`slab`,
hex), $6\times10^{-14}$ (`slab`, tet), $3\times10^{-15}$ (`layered`, hex)
and $6\times10^{-14}$ (`layered`, tet).

## Regeneration

```bash
python slab_leadfield_mms.py --emit
python slab_leadfield_mms.py --self-check
python docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py --self-check
python docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py --check-run SLAB_RUN \
    --check-run LAYERED_RUN
python docs/leadField/figures.py --mesh-case slab_hex=SLAB_HEX \
    --mesh-case slab_tet=SLAB_TET --mesh-case layered_hex=LAYERED_HEX \
    --mesh-case layered_tet=LAYERED_TET
```

`--emit` writes `reference/slab_leadfield.py` and `latex/leadfield_*.tex`. A
run is a copy of the tutorial outside the repository after
`./Allrun [-problem layered] -mesh hex|tet -N 10`. The C++ functions are
hand-written and carry no generated regions, so the generator has no
`--check`; the comparison of the NumPy module with their transcription and
the run check above are the comparisons.

# Curved conductor {#sec-shell}

## Description and limitations

A heart shell $r_1<|\mathbf x|<r_2$ between a bath ball $|\mathbf x|<r_1$
(cellZone `bloodPool`) and an outer bath $r_2<|\mathbf x|<r_3$ (cellZone
`bath`), with the transmission solution of `shell_mms.py`. The current
generated in the heart crosses both curved interfaces into the torso. The
heart conductivities are full tensors whose fibre and sheet rotate through
the wall, and the bath conductivity varies in space. The exact potential has
non-zero normal and tangential gradients on both spheres; it is continuous
across them, the extracellular flux is continuous and the intracellular
potential is sealed, all exactly.

The problem exercises the heart source with a full, varying $\mathbf G_i$, the
anisotropic heart operator, two curved heart--torso interfaces crossed by
polyhedral faces, a varying torso conductivity, and the bidomain wall
condition. It also needs data that an ordinary run does not have: a source
in every zone and a current through the outer boundary. These enter both
channels as one extra cell source (@sec-identity), so the problem verifies
the conductor and the lead fields with the manufactured data included. The
verifier uses the exact $V_m$ at the heart cell centres only; the myocardium
of the case runs one step of `BuenoOrovio`, whose $V_m$ is uniform, and the
channel on the computed $V_m$ is a check of reciprocity, not of accuracy.
The solution needs the bidomain conductor and the reference point; ground and
surface-current patches are refused.

## Problem instance

| `outerNear` | $(0.0517,\,1.0713,\,0.0811)$ | 1.076 | `bath`, next to the heart |
| `outerSide` | $(-1.2117,\,-0.4313,\,0.6271)$ | 1.431 | `bath` |

- One time step, $\Delta t=10^{-3}$; at that time $S=\sqrt{1.001}$.

In cardiacFoam:

- tutorial `manufacturedSolutions/leadFieldECG/sphericalShell`, options
  `-mesh hex|tet`, `-N`, `-seed`;
- `setManufacturedFields` writes `0/ConductivityIntracellular`,
  `0/ConductivityExtracellular` and `0/bodyAndOrgansConductivity` from the
  solution at the cell centres; every cell takes $\mathbf G_i$ and
  $\mathbf G_e$ of the heart formula, and the torso cells $\sigma_B$ of their

- ECG domain `leadFieldECG`, torso cellZones `bloodPool` and `bath`,
  `distanceWeightedHarmonic`; myocardium `bidomainSolver` with
  `sealedHeartBoundary true` and `conductivitySource field`;

## Construction

*Transmural coordinate and tensors.* The coordinate $\lambda$, the fibre
angle $\theta$, the function $\omega$, the fixed frame
$(\mathbf e_a,\mathbf e_b,\mathbf n_s)$, the fibre $\mathbf f$, the sheet
$\mathbf s$ and the two tensors are those of the sealed monodomain and
bidomain shells, with $r_1$, $r_2$ the radii of the heart:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_lambda.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_theta.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_omega.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_frame.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_fibre.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_sheet.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Gi.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Ge.tex >}}

$\mathbf G_i$ and $\mathbf G_e$ share one frame and one fibre angle. A fixed
frame is used because a fibre field tangent to a sphere vanishes somewhere
on it.

*Bath conductivity.*

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_sigmahat.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_sigmaB.tex >}}

*Smooth fields.* With

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_S.tex >}}

the smooth extracellular and intracellular fields are

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_fhat.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_hhat.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_f.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_h.tex >}}

$\hat f$ is the field $\hat h_e$ and $\hat h$ the field $\hat h_i$ of the
bidomain shell.

*Interface corrections.* On sphere $j$ ($j=1$: $|\mathbf x|=r_1$, $j=2$:
$|\mathbf x|=r_2$) the unit normal out of the heart is $\mathbf n_j$ and
$\nabla\omega=d_j\mathbf n_j$:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_n1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_n2.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_d1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_d2.tex >}}

With $\sigma_{B,1}$ the bath-ball formula and $\sigma_{B,2}$ the outer-bath
formula of $\sigma_B$, evaluated at $\mathbf x$, and $\mathbf G_i$,
$\mathbf G_e$ the heart tensors at $\mathbf x$,

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_gj.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_mj.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_g.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_m.tex >}}

In the heart $\phi=f+\omega g$ and $\phi_i=h+\omega m$, and in the bath
$\phi=f$. On sphere $j$, $\omega=0$ and $\nabla(\omega g)=g_jd_j\mathbf n_j$,
so

- $\phi$ is continuous ($f$ on both sides);
- $\mathbf n_j\cdot\mathbf G_e\nabla\phi=\mathbf n_j\cdot\mathbf G_e\nabla f+\mathbf n_j\cdot(\sigma_{B,j}\mathbf I-\mathbf G_e)\nabla f=\mathbf n_j\cdot\sigma_B\nabla\phi$;
- $\mathbf n_j\cdot\mathbf G_i\nabla\phi_i=\mathbf n_j\cdot\mathbf G_i\nabla h-\mathbf n_j\cdot\mathbf G_i\nabla h=0$.

The denominators are positive because the tensors are positive definite, so
every zone formula extends smoothly beyond its sphere, where polyhedral faces
put cell centres.

*Common mode.* The generator adds to $\phi$ and $\phi_i$ the same term,
$T$ times a field built on

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_T.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_f2.tex >}}

so that $V_m$ is unchanged. In the heart the term is $T(f_2+\omega q)$, with
$q$ sealing it with respect to $\mathbf G_i$:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_qj.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_q.tex >}}

In the bath zone of sphere $j$ it is $T(f_2+\beta_jr_j)$, with $\beta_j$ zero
on the sphere and $r_j$ the correction that keeps the extracellular flux
continuous, built with the heart tensors $\mathbf G_i^{(j)}$,
$\mathbf G_e^{(j)}$ of the sphere ($\theta=\theta_0$ for $j=1$,
$\theta=\theta_0+\theta_1$ for $j=2$) and the denominator $D_j$, positive in
the whole zone, the origin included:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_beta1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_beta2.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_rj.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_kappa.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_D1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_D2.tex >}}

The case uses $A_T=0$, so $T=0$ and the term vanishes; the
alternate parameters of the generator switch it on for the header self-test.

*Data.* The sources are the residuals of the exact fields,

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_sources.tex >}}

which is the heart equation of @sec-lf-problem with $V_m=\phi_i-\phi$, and
the outer boundary carries the exact outward current

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_gout.tex >}}

evaluated at each outer face centre with the outer-bath formula.

## Exact solution

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_phi.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_phiI.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_transmission_Vm.tex >}}

in the heart, with $g$ and $m$ linear in $S$. The verifier evaluates $\phi$
with the formula of the zone that contains the point (`zoneOf`), gauged as in
@sec-slab at the centroid $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$ of the pinned cell. The
sources are not printed: they are `phiESource` of the zone in
`expressions("levelSet")` of `shell_mms.py`. In code: `Vm`, `phiE`, `phiI`,
`gradPhiE`, `Gi`, `Ge`, `sigmaB`, `divGiGradPhiI` and `phiESource` (the source
$S_H$ or $S_T$ of the zone) of the namespace `shellTransmissionMMS`; in Python
`Model.eval_xyz(zone, name, points, t)` of `shell_mms.py`, and `shell_eval`,
`shell_phi` of `leadfield_reference.py`.

## Self-checks {#sec-shell-checks}

`shell_mms.py --self-check` runs, as `--emit` and `--write` do before they
write, and `test_shell_mms.py` repeats:

- shared construction: $\lambda$, $\omega$, the frame, the wall normals,
  $d_j$, $\mathbf G_i$, $\mathbf G_e$, $\hat h$ and $\hat f$ equal those of
  `shell_monodomain_mms.py` and `shell_bidomain_mms.py`, whose fragments are
  printed above (symbolic);
- interface conditions: continuity of $\phi$, of the extracellular flux and
  the sealing of $\phi_i$ below $10^{-12}$ at 24 points of each sphere and
  three times, in 30-digit arithmetic, for the default and the alternate
  parameters;
- sources and gradients: against fourth-order central differences
  ($h=10^{-3}$) to $10^{-6}$ relative at 40 random points, a point next to
  the origin and the origin, at two times, and with each zone formula
  evaluated $0.025$ beyond its sphere;
- boundedness and positive denominators over the zones widened by $0.05$;
- richness: on each sphere and for each tensor, the tangential part of
  $\mathbf G\mathbf n$ applied to the gradient ($\nabla\phi$ for
  $\mathbf G_e$, $\nabla\phi_i$ for $\mathbf G_i$) has an RMS of at least 0.2
  times that of the reference flux ($\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf G_e\nabla\phi$,
  $\lvert\mathbf G_i\nabla\phi_i\rvert$), and reaches 0.2 of it over at least
  70% of the area;
- the common mode leaves $V_m$, $\nabla V_m$ unchanged ($10^{-14}$), and the
  manufactured ionic closure of the heart holds ($10^{-13}$).

The verifier stops when a cell centre lies farther than its own size outside
the radial range of its cellZone, when the case conductivities differ from the
solution's at the cell centres by more than $10^{-10}$ relative, or when an
electrode lies in the heart. `leadfield_reference.py --self-check` asserts
that the twelve electrodes and the reference point lie in the zones of the
table above and that the body-surface electrodes lie at
$\lvert\mathbf x\rvert=1.495$, and `figures.py` that $\mathbf G_i$ and
$\mathbf G_e$ have the same eigenvectors. `--check-run` compares the run with
`shell_mms.py` as in @sec-slab-checks. On the tetrahedra of the figures the
gauge and the centroid values agree to $3\times10^{-16}$. On the cubed sphere
the cells are not affine and their outer faces are curved: the pinned-cell
centroid is not recomputed, and the centroid values are checked at the
six-digit centroids of the log, to $3\times10^{-6}$ at $N=8$ and $N=12$.

## Regeneration

```bash
python shell_mms.py --emit
python shell_mms.py --self-check
H=../../../src/verificationModels/bathBidomainVerification
python shell_mms.py --check $H/manufacturedShellTransmissionBathBidomainReference.H
python -m pytest test_shell_mms.py
python docs/leadField/leadfield_reference.py --check-run SHELL_RUN
python docs/leadField/figures.py --mesh-case shell_hex=SHELL_HEX \
    --mesh-case shell_tet=SHELL_TET
```

`--emit` writes `latex/shell_transmission_*.tex`; the shared fragments
`latex/shell_*.tex` and `latex/shell_bidomain_G*.tex` are those of
`shell_monodomain_mms.py` and `shell_bidomain_mms.py`. The generator emits no
NumPy module: `leadfield_reference.py` evaluates the fields through
`Model.eval_xyz` of `shell_mms.py`. `--write PATH` rewrites the whole header,
including a table of self-test samples that the cardiacFoam verifiers compare
with their compiled functions.

# The lead-field identity and the static rows {#sec-identity}

## Description and limitations

Both problems compare the lead-field channel with a direct solve of the same
discrete conductor, and both with the exact potential. The comparison with
the direct solve is algebraic: it holds on any mesh to the tolerance of the
fixed points, and it checks the adjoint, not the discretisation. The
comparison with the exact potential measures the discretisation of the
conductor and the recording at a cell.

## The identity

The finite-volume conductor is a linear system $A\boldsymbol\phi=\mathbf b(V_m)$
over all cells, with the reference cell pinned to $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and
$\mathbf b=-\nabla_h\cdot(\mathbf G_i\nabla_hV_m)$ in heart cells and zero in
torso cells, both per unit volume. $A=M+C$, with $M$ the implicit symmetric
part and $C$ the explicit corrections (cross diffusion, non-orthogonal and
interface terms). For electrode $e$, `buildLeadFields` solves the adjoint
problem

$$
A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf z_e=\mathbf e_{c(e)},
\qquad\text{as the fixed point}\quad M\mathbf z_e=\mathbf e_{c(e)}-C^{\mathsf T}\mathbf z_e,
$$

and the channel is

$$
\phi_e=\sum_c z_{e,c}\,V_c\,b_c(V_m)+c_e
=\phi_{c(e)}\quad\text{of the converged forward solve},
$$

with $c_e$ the constant contribution of ground values, surface currents
(the layered problem) and a non-zero reference value. In the curved
conductor the manufactured data enter as one more cell source,

$$
s_c=S_c-\frac1{V_c}\sum_{f\in\partial c\cap\partial\Omega}g_{\mathrm{out},f}\lvert\mathbf S_f\rvert,
\qquad
s\leftarrow s-\frac{\sum_cV_cs_c}{\sum_cV_c},
$$

with $S_c$ the zone source $S_H$ or $S_T$ at the cell centre and the
outer-face current moved into the owner cell; its volume mean is removed so
that the pure-Neumann problem is consistent. The direct solve adds $s$ to
$\mathbf b$ and the channel adds $\sum_cz_{e,c}V_cs_c$.

## What is compared

At each sample the verifier writes, per electrode (the body-surface
electrodes and the interior probes alike):

| column | meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `leadField` | the channel $\phi_e$ on the computed $V_m$ |
| `direct` | the forward solve of the same conductor on the computed $V_m$, assembly and solve repeated until the relative change is below `leadFieldFixedPoint tolerance`, in cell $c(e)$ |
| `exactPoint` | $\phi(\mathbf r_e,t)$, gauged at $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$ |
| `exactCentroid` | $\phi(\mathbf x_{c(e)},t)$, gauged at $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$ |
| `leadFieldStatic` | the channel on the exact $V_m$ at the heart cell centres (plus $\mathbf s$ in the curved conductor) |
| `directStatic` | the direct solve on the same exact $V_m$ (and $\mathbf s$) |

and the summary rows (L1, L2 and maximum over the samples, per electrode and
as the maximum over the electrodes):

- `leadField-direct` and `leadField-direct_relative` (divided by the largest
  $|$`direct`$|$): the reciprocity gap;
- `leadFieldStatic-directStatic`: the same gap on the exact $V_m$;
- `leadFieldStatic-exactPoint`, `leadFieldStatic-exactCentroid`,
  `directStatic-exactPoint`, `directStatic-exactCentroid`: the error against
  the exact potential at the electrode point and at the electrode-cell
  centroid, in the gauge of the conductor's reference point;
- `localisation` $=$ `exactPoint` $-$ `exactCentroid`: the part of the point
  error that comes from recording a cell value at a point inside the cell. It
  is zero in the slab (constant torso potential) and first order in the cell
  size otherwise;
- `phiStatic`, `phiStatic_heart`, `phiStatic_torso`,
  `phiStatic_interfaceBand`, `phiStatic_surface`: mean, volume-weighted RMS
  and maximum of `directStatic` against the exact potential at every cell
  centre, over all cells, the heart, the torso, the cells with a
  heart--torso face and the cells with a face on the outer boundary of the
  conductor. The last region holds the cells of the body-surface electrodes,
  so `phiStatic_surface` is the error of the direct solve over the whole body
  surface, of which the electrodes sample eight cells.

The static rows use the exact $V_m$, so their error is that of the passive
conductor and of the recording alone, not of the myocardium solve. The
verifier treats every electrode alike; the summarisers of the studies
(`setup/studies/summarize.py` of each case) report the body-surface
electrodes, the interior probes and `phiStatic_surface` as separate groups.

## Checks

`buildLeadFields` stops with a fatal error when the probed explicit operator
is not linear or does not reproduce the assembled one ($10^{-11}$), when
$\langle\mathbf z,C\boldsymbol\psi\rangle\ne\langle C^{\mathsf T}\mathbf z,\boldsymbol\psi\rangle$
or $M$ is not symmetric ($10^{-12}$), when the residual of a lead field
exceeds $10^{-8}$, or when the pinned row is not satisfied ($10^{-8}$); it
refuses nonlinear schemes. `leadFieldECG` stops when the signature of the
lead fields (mesh, conductivities, schemes, electrodes, reference) differs
from the case.
